reason: The right page's horizontal call-path diagram is clean and readable on desktop, while the left diagram is tall with tangled, crossing connector lines.
The right page has a cleaner numbered sequence diagram, a proportional timing bar and better-organized callouts, though its phone diagram needs a sideways swipe.
The right flowchart is clearer with color-coded lanes and cleaner routing, and its time-limit cards and who-is-called cards are more scannable than the left's cramped boxes and sparse layout.

The left page has a compact, legible horizontal pipeline diagram plus a to-scale link-capacity bar chart, whereas the right diagram is a tall, sprawling vertical layout with long wandering connectors.
The right architecture diagram is compact and well labeled with a stacked regional box and a to-scale scaling bar chart, while the left diagram is a tall vertical layout with long looping connectors.
The left page has a clear options comparison table, large labeled to-scale bars and a well-structured recommendation, while the right is plainer and its range and cost charts are tiny.
The right range chart is clean and unobstructed and its risks table and phone layout are tidy, while the left chart has the goal line colliding with value labels and its option cards wrap awkwardly.

The left page is richer and more polished, with a highlighted comparison table, large to-scale fee bars and a clear freeze timeline, despite a truncated bar-chart caption and a label sitting on the freeze line.

The right page has a more polished layout with labeled option badges, a larger to-scale cost chart, can/cannot cards and clear recommendation cards, whereas the left has overflowing option cards and a small chart.

The left page has large, clearly labeled range and timeline charts with direct value labels and a clean numbered recommendation, while the right charts are tiny with little labeling and a plainer layout.
